declared_proposition: Let F' refine a held-out fold F. Fit positive scales alpha outside F and beta outside F'. On F', e(beta)=e(alpha)+(alpha-beta)w, so Minkowski gives ||e(beta)||_p <= ||e(alpha)||_p+|alpha-beta|||w||_p. If the right side is below beta min_{i in F'}w_i, every count on F' is positive. This is an exact refinement-stability certificate for cross-fitted support.
mathematical_argument: The vector identity is coordinatewise and Minkowski is exact. If some held-out count A_j were zero, then |e_j(beta)|=beta w_j is at least the zero barrier, contradicting the strict norm bound. The audit uses rational scales and outward-rounded rational eighth roots. All 140 nested bridges q=2 to 4 to 8 to 16 pass on five finite dyadic blocks. Their inputs still use enumerated Goldbach counts, so this does not supply the required cofinal arithmetic estimate.

discarded_route: promoting finite success under increasingly fine folds to a cofinal Goldbach theorem
remaining_gap: No cofinal analytic estimate controls the parent residual norm and scale-refit drift without enumerating Goldbach representations.
